Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroTech Dynamics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroTech Dynamics' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Jane Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Lawson, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Berger, Chief Strategy Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

John Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning. AeroTech Dynamics delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aerospace, defense, and services. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Today, we'll cover key areas including the expansion of our service offerings and customer base, key assumptions underlying our guidance, performance of our priority defense programs, the defense budget outlook and its impact on our company, analysis of our gross margins, operating margins, and net income, revenue performance by segment, our updated revenue and earnings guidance for the full year, and backlog growth.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our AeroSync program and its potential to transform sustainment through AI-driven predictive analytics, reducing maintenance events and unlocking higher-margin recurring revenues. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily.

With that, I'll turn it over to Jane for the financial details.

Jane Harlan:
Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. Let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $18.5 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $2.85. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $12 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains on track at $88-92 billion in revenue and adjusted EPS of $13.50-$14.50, and we're actively managing costs while investing in key growth initiatives. We're also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Specific financial highlights include gross margin of 18.7%, operating income of $2.45 billion, and free cash flow of $2.5 billion.

Let me provide more depth across our key areas, starting with revenue by segment: commercial aerospace, defense, and services. Consolidated revenues hit $18.5 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with a book-to-bill of 1.25x supporting our robust backlog. Commercial aerospace, at 42% of revenues or $7.8 billion, grew 18% YoY, driven by OEM ramps on Boeing 737 MAX and Airbus A320neo programs, with 1,200 unit deliveries up 22%, nacelle and thrust reverser lines at full rate in Seattle and Hamburg. Supply chain mitigations cut titanium lead times 15%, GTF aftermarket up 25% from Pratt & Whitney issues, North America 55% of growth, APAC 30% from IndiGo and Air India, Europe 12%. Margins hit 14.2% with hybrid-electric propulsion investments targeting 20-50 seat regionals.

Defense, 38% of revenues at $7.0 billion, up 9% YoY, anchored by F-35 LRIP Lot 15/16 at $1.2 billion, hypersonics and CCA adding $450 million, international F-35 to Finland/Switzerland, Eurofighter upgrades. North America up 11%, Europe 7% on NATO pledges, Middle East stable. Fixed-price contracts at 12% EBITDA, space now 8% hedging fighters, backlog $28 billion up 10%.

Services, highest-margin at 20% or $3.7 billion, up 14% YoY, MRO surging 20% on LEAP/GEnx commercial engines, 12% on Black Hawk/Chinook defense. Mobile MRO at 15 sites including RAAF, 95% utilization across 12 depots, GADx AR/VR cutting times 30%, margins 22.5% up 300 bps. EMEA +18%, North America +13%, LATAM emerging.

Next, gross margin, operating margin, and net income analysis. Adjusted gross margin reached 18.7%, up 150 bps YoY from 17.2% and 80 bps sequentially, strongest in two years, tracking to full-year 18.0-18.5% midpoint. Segment mix added 90 bps: Defense Systems 62% of revenue at $11.5 billion, margins 20.1% up from 18.5% on C-130J/Black Hawk aftermarket, DoD IDIQs in missile defense. Commercial Aviation 28% or $5.2 billion at 16.8%, Boeing/Airbus stabilization offset by titanium issues. Space & Launch 10% or $1.85 billion at 17.5%, NASA Artemis and Vulcan. ECRP saved $120 million via LEAN in Oklahoma/Alabama, supplier FPAs with Honeywell/RTX cut inflation 4%, headwinds $45 million on Navy sub labor shortages. Q4 to 19.2% with F-35 LRIP and MBSE.

Operating margin hit 13.2%, up 220 bps YoY, SG&A 4.1%, R&D 2.8% on directed energy/autonomy. $200 million indirect cuts from consolidations, AME robotics up throughput 25% on 787 spars. Operating income $2.45 billion, EBITDA 16.5%. U.S. contracts 70%, international 14.5% on Middle East Patriots.

Net income $850 million or $2.45 EPS wait no, aligning to $2.85 adjusted, up 31% YoY, tax 21.5%, interest $55 million offset by refinancing. Pivot to sustainment 45% backlog, $500 million supply chain resiliency.

Turning to expansion of service offerings and customer base, a key growth driver transforming to higher-margin recurring revenues. Services segment grew 28% YoY to $1.45 billion wait scaling to our size ~$5B+, 32% of backlog up from 24%, via MRO, digital engineering, PBL, cyber sustainment using AeroSync AI/edge computing with Palantir, cutting F-16/Eurofighter maintenance 35%. Q3 secured $2.8 billion IDIQs including $1.2 billion USAF C-130J PBL, margins 18.2% vs products 9.5%. Hypersonics sustainment post-DARPA OTA for ARRW-like boosters, $15B market; CyberShield $450 million Space Force sats, $25B space TAM.

Customer diversification: U.S. DoD 55% down from 68%, international 42% growth from AUKUS/GCAP/NATO 2%. Indo-Pacific RAAF $900M F-35 via Melbourne MRO up 20%, APAC $620M up 45% on F-15J/Tejas. Europe $510M up 32% Hellenic Patriot/Polish Black Hawk. Middle East 15% backlog via Saudi GIDE drones $300M. Commercial $150M Southwest 737 MAX. Aligns with $100B+ global sustainment on aging fleets avg 28 years, OTAs/SBIR, 85% multi-year recurring, book-to-bill 1.4x, backlog $28B up 22% 60% funded. FY24 services 25-30% growth to 40% revenues by 2026, $250M capex Huntsville/Singapore, risks FX/CRs.

On backlog growth, total $210 billion up $28 billion or 15% YoY, $128 billion funded up 14%. Funded $128B, book-to-bill 1.28x. Aeronautics 42% $88B up 15% on F-35 Lot 16 $1.8B, NGAD $450M, FMS Australia/Japan $650M. Missiles 18.5% growth to $40B on hypersonics $1.2B ARRW/LRHW, interceptors $500M. Space $25B up 9.8% Artemis $700M, ESS $300M, Starshield $150M. U.S. 85% up 14.6%, international 28% YoY Middle East/Asia/Europe FCAS $400M. Digital twins/additive cut times 20-30%, pipeline $120B. H2 10-12% growth.

Updated revenue and earnings guidance: Raising FY24 revenue to $32.5-34.0B wait aligning overall $88-92B, EPS $13.50-14.50 wait to $15.20-16.00 midpoint 14% growth, op margins 13.0-13.5%. Commercial $11.5-12.0B up 22% RPKs +5%, MRO 28%, LEAP. Defense $15-15.8B up 10% F-35 $1.2B, hypersonics Dark Eagle, FMS $800M. Space $6-6.2B up 15% Artemis/GPS IIIF. FCF $3.8-4.2B, capex $1.2B Fort Worth/Huntsville. Inflation 4-5% passthrough, regions NA 70%, EMEA 18%, APAC 12%. IR&D $950M AI CCA/DEW, M&A $500M cyber.

Key assumptions underpin this: FY24 $88-92B revenue, EPS $13.50-14.50, Defense 55% $145B backlog, DoD $850B FY25 +2-3% procurement/RDT&E, F-35 120-130 LRIP to 156 FRP, TR-3 <$500M growth, intl $4-5B. Missiles hypersonics $2.8B IOC Q4'26, PAC-3/JASSM 2500/qtr. Middle East $3B Patriot/THAAD oil sens, Europe GCAP $6B. Supply titanium $25-28/kg, inflation 2.5-3%, 70/30 contract mix. Commercial Boeing 38/mo 737, 5/mo 787, A320 50/mo, GTF $1.1B Q4 recov 20% '25, LEAP $2.5B, RPK 5-6%, Asia 25%. Space Artemis mid'26 $4.2B, Vulcan 75%, sats $1.5B, PWSA $2B. FX USD +2% EUR, capex $1.8B, FCF $8-9B. Sens +1% DoD +$300M rev, Boeing delay -2%, titanium +10% -$150M EBIT. M&A $12B autonomy.

These reflect $250B backlog, geo tailwinds, commercial upcycle.

Mike Harlan:
Thank you, Jane. Operationally, we've improved supply chain management, increasing production on F-35, hypersonics, drawing from titanium stabilization via Japan/Kazakhstan reroutes, dual-sourcing Hexcel, domestic with Allegheny/IperionX, robotic layup/advanced manufacturing boosting throughput 25%, digital twins/MBSE cutting ECOs 15%, lean sigma $500M cost-out, high 95% MRO utilization, no major labor disruptions beyond IAM risks, attrition to 5%.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. Technologically, strides in next-gen propulsion including hypersonic boost-glide GPI Mach7+ 90% hit-to-kill White Sands, HAWC-derived Lot2 $2.4B MDA, C/C composites derisked 15% cost cut, TRL7 quantum comms/DEWs 300kW HELIOS DDG quals $200M, autonomy CCA XQ-58A 50+hrs AFRL demos, AI Mosaic battlespace, RD-180 Vulcan successors $350M, optical payloads proliferated LEO, hypersonic reentry X-37B, digital thread wing lifecycle 15% O&M cut, additive 20% titanium.

Tom Berger:
Thank you, Elena. Strategically, evaluating acquisitions like autonomy leaders akin Anduril for CCA/NGAD integration, tuck-ins Quantum Dynamics cyber, $12B war chest/$500M dry powder, new models sustainment tilt 85% recurring, Fortress Forward intl FMS 22%, offsets Qatar/Romania, 30% domestic NDAA, JADC2 mesh AI $350M R&D, Replicator attritables thousands by '25.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Tom. Marketing-wise, new branding resonates targeting DoD primes, allies, commercials, digital channels boosting awareness, success in APAC/Europe campaigns tied to AUKUS/GCAP wins, results show 25% lead gen increase, 20% brand lift per surveys.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Lisa. On compliance, robust CMMC 2.0 cybersecurity, zero-trust CyberShield, supply chain audits mitigating rare earths/gallium nitride, EAC 98% accuracy fixed-price 60%, FX hedges.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the backlog growth, absolute and percent change?

John Reynolds:
Certainly, Alex. Our total backlog stands at $210 billion, up $28 billion absolutely or 15% year-over-year and 13% sequentially from $182 billion prior quarter, well above our 10-15% target with book-to-bill 1.28x. Funded portion $128 billion up 14%, unfunded $82 billion on IDIQ/multi-year. Conversion 35% next 12 months, 65% in 24. Aeronautics $88 billion up 15% on F-35 Lot 16 $1.8 billion, NGAD early packages $450 million, FMS sustainment Australia/Japan $650 million AUKUS/Indo-Pacific. Missiles fastest 18.5% to $40 billion, hypersonics $1.2 billion ARRW/LRHW, MDA interceptors $500 million Ukraine/Red Sea, book-to-bill 1.45x. Space $25 billion up 9.8%, Artemis Orion $700 million, Space Force ESS $300 million protected waveforms, Starshield $150 million SpaceX. U.S. 85% $178 billion up 14.6% FY24 NDAA $886 billion R&D highs, international $32 billion up 28% FMS Middle East MQ-9, Asia MRFA, Europe FCAS sensor fusion $400 million. $500 million YTD digital/additive investments cut lead times 20-30%, 15% throughput gain, $120 billion pipeline 45% win rate JADC2/CCA. H2 another 10-12% growth supports FY24 revenue/EPS.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Ben Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Hi, I'm curious about the key assumptions underlying the guidance?

Jane Harlan:
Ben, great question. Our FY24 guidance of $88-92 billion revenue, $13.50-14.50 adjusted EPS, Defense EBIT 11-12%, Commercial 9-10%, Space 12-13%, FCF $8-9 billion with $2.2 billion pensions, and initial FY25 $93-99 billion revenue up 6-8%, EPS $14.50-15.50. Defense 55%, $145 billion backlog: DoD FY25 $850 billion PBR +4.1% topline 1.9% real, +2-3% procurement/RDT&E, $60-70 billion supplements Ukraine/Israel. F-35 120-130 LRIP Lot15-17, FRP Lot18 156 CY25, TR-3 <$500 million growth, NATO FMS Finland/Poland/Romania $4-5 billion 85% prob. Hypersonics Army LRHW/AF ARRW $2.8 billion FY25 IOC Q4'26, PAC-3 MSE $1.2 billion Japan/Australia/Ukraine, JASSM/JDAM 2500 units/qtr post-replen. Middle East Saudi Vision $3 billion Patriot/THAAD 20% oil sens >$90, Europe NATO 2% GCAP BAE/Leonardo $6 billion. Titanium $25-28/kg Japan/Kazakh, no IAM strikes Alabama F-35, inflation 2.5-3% labor/composites, 70/30 FFP/incentive. Commercial 30%: Boeing 737 MAX 38/mo YE24, 787 5/mo H1'25, Airbus A320neo 50/mo nacelle/wing +12%. P&W GTF inspections 600+ engines $1.1 billion Q4, 20% MRO recov '25, CFM LEAP $2.5 billion 85% dispatch, RPK 5-6% IATA narrowbody 11.5 hrs/day, leasing LIBOR+ stable or 10-15 bps if Fed>4%, Asia IndiGo/Air India 25% growth China 95% pre-COVID, US LCC Southwest 10% MAX delay '26. Digital twin wings 15% O&M cut, additive 20% Ti brackets 40% lead cut, SAF 6% +5% pricing. Space 15% 10-12% CAGR: Artemis III mid'26 $4.2 billion SLS/Orion, ULA Vulcan 75% post-Atlas RD-180 succ $350 million, sats $1.5 billion optical 2000+ LEO OneWeb/AST, PWSA DoD $2 billion missile warning, ESA Ariane6 10/yr 30% propulsion, ISR drones Ukraine/Taiwan $800 million. Cross: FX USD +2% EUR/GBP +5% JPY -8% rev, inflation 2.5% labor 4%, capex $1.8 billion Palmdale NGAD, FCF $10 billion F-35 milestones $3 billion receivables, pension Q2'25. Sens: DoD +1% +$300 million rev, Boeing MAX to42/mo '25 -2% comm growth, ti +10% -$150M EBIT +$500M lean offset. M&A $12 billion Anduril-like CCA/NGAD, 30% domestic NDAA.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Chris Lee:
Regarding the performance of priority defense programs?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Chris, happy to unpack. Priority defense generated $11.5 billion Q3 revenue up 18% YoY 22% seq, 62% total rev, adj op margins 13.2% +120 bps on LRIP volume, fixed-price mix, $145 million favorable adjustments underruns. NGAD family on FY24 risk reduction, X-47 85% 150-hr Nevada tests, $1.2 billion digital engineering AF RCO, backlog $18.5 billion 1.4x book-to-bill, margins 11.8% CCA autonomy MBSE -25% timelines, AUKUS $5-7 billion exports post-F-35. Hypersonics HAWC GPI end-to-end White Sands Mach7+ 90% hit-kill, rev $650M up32% $2.4B MDA Lot2 sole-source, C/C Hexcel in-house -15% unit cost, margins 14.5%, FY25 NDAA $4.7B +20% LRIP Q4'25 200 units/yr FRP'28. Rotary/missile VH-92A 12 deliveries 6mo early zero OT&E defs $420M up25% $900M FRP increase, PrSM Inc2 >500km autonomous seeker live-fire success, backlog $3.2B intl Poland $450M PDA UAE LOI 300+ Red Sea. U.S. DoD 85% rev, Ukraine supp $1.1B MQ-9 ISR/sustain, Indo-Pac India P-8I $800M up40% AEW&C PLAN, NATO 12% bookings UK/Norway F-35 C4ISR $1.5B APG-85 AESA 30% track-scan. Challenges rare earth GaN MMIC inflation mitigated stockpiling Lockheed co-prod +3% vs industry +7%. DE 300kW HELIOS laser DDG quals $200M. Q4 $12.5-13B rev FY growth 16-18% margins 12.8-13.3%, record $52B backlog 2.8yr vis, $350M FY25 R&D JADC2 AI mesh NGAD/GPI/space. Geopolitics 5-7% CAGR $120B TAM 15-20% share.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Dana Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Dana Patel:
Question about the defense budget outlook and impact on company?

Tom Berger:
Dana, key point. We derive 72% FY24 rev from DoD/allies, funded backlog $128B up14% total $210B. Global spend $2.44T '23 SIPRI +6.8% steepest post-Cold War, 4-5% CAGR GPC China/Russia, NATO 23/32 >2% GDP vs 3 '14. U.S. FY25 PBR $849.8B +4.1% 1.9% real, R&D $145B +2.2%, Proc $168B flat high-end, O&M $317B +4.3% readiness. NDAA bipartisan $850-860B+, Replicator attritables thousands '25, NGAD $2.7B RDT&E demos. Europe Steadfast Defender €230B surge post'22, Poland $10B F-35 Germany €100B, Lockheed partner, Ukraine $175B aid JASSM/Stormbreaker +25% Q3. APAC China $296B +7.2% 370ships hypersonics, Japan ¥8.5T F-35B GPI, AUKUS SSN subs propulsors/combat, Middle East Israel Iron Dome Saudi $60B F-15EX. Q3 defense rev $13.4B up11% bookings $19B 1.4x, FY $16.8-17.2B +9-11% margins 12.8% +50bps. Fighters F-35 Lot17 $4.1B avionics/EW TR-3 Block4 $10.5B 18% flyaway, NGAD Digital Skunk Works $1-2B/yr post-Milestone B '26. Munitions FY25 PBR LRASM $550M x2 hypersonics $1.2B ARRW test, Camden cap x2 200+/yr '26. Unmanned Replicator $1B XQ-58A Valkyrie CCA AFRL IDIQ $5B. Space PWSA Transport $1.8B optical comms EWAAC $2.9B. Fortress Forward: FMS 22% up15% offsets Qatar F-15QA Romania F-16, sustainment F-35 PBL $25B 40yr, tech $850M capex AI/ML Mosaic DEW counter-drone 20% CAGR, supply ti domestic Allegheny. Risks CR delay $15-20B but 7+yr vis funded, inflation pass 85% CP, FFP 60% 98% EAC. Structural positive peer tech hypersonics/autonomy/JADC2, 8-10% organic to '27 defense EPS $2.10-2.30.

John Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
